Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Find lost guideline – _____ getting lost under an overhead
Diving procedures.fact: Recovery from accidental inversion in dry suit – Avoid uncontrolled ascent following unintended flow of gas to the feet of a dry suit. Follow guideline in silt-out – Avoid getting lost under an overhead.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Cross break in guideline – _____ the guideline on the other side of a break to avoid getting lost under an overhead
Diving procedures.fact: Find lost guideline – Avoid getting lost under an overhead. Cross break in guideline – Find the guideline on the other side of a break to avoid getting lost under an overhead.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Lost mask ascent – _____ when the diver's vision is impaired by not having a mask
Diving procedures.fact: Emergency ascents – Procedures for reaching the surface in various emergencies. Lost mask ascent – Ascent when the diver's vision is impaired by not having a mask.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Lost buoyancy ascent – _____ when the diver's buoyancy is compromised
Diving procedures.fact: Emergency ascents – Procedures for reaching the surface in various emergencies. Lost mask ascent – Ascent when the diver's vision is impaired by not having a mask.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Assisted ascents – _____ where the diver in distress is assisted by another diver
Diving procedures.fact: Assisted ascents – Ascents where the diver in distress is assisted by another diver.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Buoyant ascent – _____ positive buoyancy to rise to the surface
Diving procedures.fact: Buoyant ascent – Using positive buoyancy to rise to the surface.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Lost weights ascent with flare – _____ of an incident where the diver cannot neutralise positive buoyancy
Diving procedures.fact: Lost weights ascent with flare – Mitigation of an incident where the diver cannot neutralise positive buoyancy.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Controlled buoyant emergency ascent – _____ control of buoyancy to ascend at an acceptably safe rate
Diving procedures.fact: Controlled buoyant emergency ascent – Fine control of buoyancy to ascend at an acceptably safe rate.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Tethered buoyant emergency ascent – _____ with positive buoyancy and depth controlled by a reel line attached to the bottom
Diving procedures.fact: Buoyant ascent – Using positive buoyancy to rise to the surface. Lost weights ascent with flare – Mitigation of an incident where the diver cannot neutralise positive buoyancy.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Free ascent – _____ where the diver has no source of breathing gas available
Diving procedures.fact: Controlled buoyant emergency ascent – Fine control of buoyancy to ascend at an acceptably safe rate. Tethered buoyant emergency ascent – Ascent with positive buoyancy and depth controlled by a reel line attached to the bottom.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Controlled emergency swimming ascent – _____ where there may be a small amount of breathing gas which becomes available due to ambient pressure reduction
Diving procedures.fact: Tethered buoyant emergency ascent – Ascent with positive buoyancy and depth controlled by a reel line attached to the bottom. Emergency swimming ascents – Emergency ascent where the diver actively swims upward at approximately neutral buoyancy.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Ditch weights to establish buoyancy – _____ of some or all ballast weights to establish neutral or positive buoyancy underwater, or to establish positive buoyancy at the surface
Diving procedures.fact: Ditch weights to establish buoyancy – Removal of some or all ballast weights to establish neutral or positive buoyancy underwater, or to establish positive buoyancy at the surface.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: In-water recompression – _____ underwater to treat decompression illness or to compensate for omitted decompression
Diving procedures.fact: Therapeutic recompression – The use of recompression to treat symptomatic decompression illness. In-water recompression – Recompression underwater to treat decompression illness or to compensate for omitted decompression.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Bailout to scuba – _____ to scuba emergency gas supply
Diving procedures.fact: Standardised emergency procedures used with manifolded twin scuba cylinders – Closing the isolation valve, or closing the left or right cylinder valves to identify and isolate a malfunction, and opening the valves as appropriate to make best use of remaining gas, and switching demand valves as required. Bailout to scuba – Switching to scuba emergency gas supply.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Bailout to pneumo hose – _____ the pneumofathometer hose as an emergency gas supply
Diving procedures.fact: Bailout to pneumo hose – Using the pneumofathometer hose as an emergency gas supply.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Abandon wet bell – _____ from wet bell which cannot be raised
Diving procedures.fact: Switch to bell onboard gas – Switch to emergency on-board gas supply in case of surface supply failure or contamination. Abandon wet bell – Surface from wet bell which cannot be raised.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Respond to heating water malfunction – _____ thermal imbalance due to inappropriate heating water temperature
Diving procedures.fact: Respond to heating water malfunction – Manage thermal imbalance due to inappropriate heating water temperature. Respond to dry suit flood – Manage insulation and buoyancy loss due to flooded dry suit.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Respond to dry suit flood – _____ insulation and buoyancy loss due to flooded dry suit
Diving procedures.fact: Respond to heating water malfunction – Manage thermal imbalance due to inappropriate heating water temperature. Respond to dry suit flood – Manage insulation and buoyancy loss due to flooded dry suit.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Respond to suit blowup – _____ uncontrolled buoyant ascent
Diving procedures.fact: Respond to suit blowup – Prevent uncontrolled buoyant ascent. Respond to buoyancy compensator blowup – Prevent uncontrolled buoyant ascent.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Respond to voice communications failure – _____ to rope signals
Diving procedures.fact: Respond to voice communications failure – Revert to rope signals.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Manage vomiting in the helmet – _____ a helmet or full-face mask after vomiting inside it before breathing from the demand valve
Diving procedures.fact: Manage vomiting in the helmet – Clear a helmet or full-face mask after vomiting inside it before breathing from the demand valve.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Manage a broken faceplate – _____ flooding of the helmet is a life-threatening emergency
Diving procedures.fact: Manage a broken faceplate – Unrestricted flooding of the helmet is a life-threatening emergency.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Bell abandonment – _____ from a disabled wet bell
Diving procedures.fact: Bell abandonment – Surfacing from a disabled wet bell.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Surface gas supply failure – _____ over to on board gas supply by bellman in the event of a surface gas supply failure
Diving procedures.fact: Bell gas panel operation – The bell gas panel is used to switch to on-board gas supply if the surface supply is compromised. Surface gas supply failure – Switch over to on board gas supply by bellman in the event of a surface gas supply failure.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Contaminated surface gas supply – _____ over to on board gas supply by bellman in the event of suspected contamination of the surface gas supply
Diving procedures.fact: Surface gas supply failure – Switch over to on board gas supply by bellman in the event of a surface gas supply failure. Contaminated surface gas supply – Switch over to on board gas supply by bellman in the event of suspected contamination of the surface gas supply.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Dynamic positioning alarm and runout response – _____ return to the bell and prepare for immediate ascent
Diving procedures.fact: Dynamic positioning alarm and runout response – Divers return to the bell and prepare for immediate ascent. Loss of bell internal pressure – Response depends on where the bell is at the time, and may include deployment of a second bell to rescue the divers.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Loss of bell internal pressure – _____ depends on where the bell is at the time, and may include deployment of a second bell to rescue the divers
Diving procedures.fact: Dynamic positioning alarm and runout response – Divers return to the bell and prepare for immediate ascent. Loss of bell internal pressure – Response depends on where the bell is at the time, and may include deployment of a second bell to rescue the divers.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Main lifting wire/winch failure – _____ lifting possibilities include the clump weight winch, other hoisting equipment on the platform, and if rated for lifting, the bell umbilical
Diving procedures.fact: Main lifting wire/winch failure – Alternative lifting possibilities include the clump weight winch, other hoisting equipment on the platform, and if rated for lifting, the bell umbilical.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Freeing the trapped casualty – _____ an entrapped or snagged diver to get free
Diving procedures.fact: Freeing the trapped casualty – Assisting an entrapped or snagged diver to get free.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Managing a convulsing casualty – _____ a diver who is convulsing underwater to the surface
Diving procedures.fact: Managing a convulsing casualty – Recovering a diver who is convulsing underwater to the surface.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Bringing the casualty to the surface – _____ the diver to a place where first aid is possible
Diving procedures.fact: Bringing the casualty to the surface – Getting the diver to a place where first aid is possible. Carrying out artificial ventilation in the water – Towing the casualty – Getting the casualty to a place where they can be taken out of the water.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Carrying out artificial ventilation in the water – Towing the casualty – _____ the casualty to a place where they can be taken out of the water
Diving procedures.fact: Bringing the casualty to the surface – Getting the diver to a place where first aid is possible. Carrying out artificial ventilation in the water – Towing the casualty – Getting the casualty to a place where they can be taken out of the water.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Controlled buoyant lift – _____ an incapacitated diver to the surface
Diving procedures.fact: Controlled buoyant lift – Lifting an incapacitated diver to the surface.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Making the casualty buoyant on the surface – _____ that the diver does not sink before they can be removed from the water
Diving procedures.fact: Making the casualty buoyant on the surface – Ensuring that the diver does not sink before they can be removed from the water.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Umbilical changeout – _____ a problematic umbilical for a replacement under water
Diving procedures.fact: Umbilical changeout – Swapping a problematic umbilical for a replacement under water.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Rescue of the working diver – _____ the disabled working diver to a place of relative safety
Diving procedures.fact: Carrying out artificial ventilation in the water – Towing the casualty – Getting the casualty to a place where they can be taken out of the water. Rescue of the working diver – Getting the disabled working diver to a place of relative safety.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Rescue of an incapacitated diver – _____ the diver to the surface
Diving procedures.fact: Carrying out artificial ventilation in the water – Towing the casualty – Getting the casualty to a place where they can be taken out of the water. Rescue of the working diver – Getting the disabled working diver to a place of relative safety.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Rescue of an unconscious diver – _____ an unconscious surface supplied diver to the surface
Diving procedures.fact: Rescue of the working diver – Getting the disabled working diver to a place of relative safety. Rescue of an incapacitated diver – Getting the diver to the surface.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Rescue of divers from a disabled closed bell – _____-water transfer to another closed bell
Diving procedures.fact: Rescue of divers from a disabled closed bell – Through-water transfer to another closed bell.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Lost bell procedures – _____ and lifting a closed bell when the lifting cables and umbilical have been severed
Diving procedures.fact: Lost bell procedures – Locating and lifting a closed bell when the lifting cables and umbilical have been severed.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Descent and ascent ��� _____ the bell to working depth and raising it at the end of the dive, with appropriate in-water decompression stops
Diving procedures.fact: Descent and ascent ��� Lowering the bell to working depth and raising it at the end of the dive, with appropriate in-water decompression stops.
